text:
Research supports separating observable evidence from inferred intent. [Herlihy et al. (2024)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/on-overcoming-miscalibrated-conversational-priors-in-llm-based-chatbots/?lang=zh-cn) find that recommendation chatbots mishandle underspecified requests through incorrect assumptions; clarification policies can improve decisions. [Zhang et al. (RecSys 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03248) evaluate recommendation-explanation judges against actual user feedback and third-party annotations, supporting human calibration rather than assuming automated judgments reflect users.

Suggested annotation scheme—a synthesis, not an established taxonomy: attach title/description evidence spans to each claim; label it supported, contradicted, or unknown. Record explicit compatibility conflicts only when documented specifications conflict. Separate a documented prerequisite from whether the user satisfies it: absence from history means unknown. Treat similar purchases as possible redundancy, never proof of current ownership or satisfied demand. For media, distinguish specific entity/edition/format matches from broad thematic similarity; neither establishes present intent. Keep factual compatibility and inferred desirability as separate judgments.

[Trust or Escalate (ICLR 2025)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/08dabd5345b37fffcbe335bd578b15a0-Paper-Conference.pdf) calibrates selective judging on human labels, trading coverage for controlled disagreement under its assumptions. Applied here: independently annotate examples across all four categories, preserve disagreements about intent, adjudicate factual conflicts, and report per-type agreement, precision, abstention rate, and coverage on separate validation annotations. A [2026 abstention-aware verification preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14189) offers an adjacent method: decompose claims into minimal conditions and audit evidence before supporting, refuting, or abstaining. Its scientific-domain findings require validation before transfer to recommendation diagnosis.
